title: Runner requirements profile
description: One project's package requirements, consumed by scripts/render.py to emit cloud-init/user-data.yaml and ansible/vars/generated.yml. Unknown keys are a hard error: a typo in a copied profile must fail loudly instead of being silently ignored. Top-level keys starting with x- are ignored anchor containers: they exist only to hold `&anchor` values for `<<:` merges in the same file and are otherwise ignored.

^x-.description: Ignored anchor container, e.g. `x-base: &base {...}` merged later with `<<: *base`. Never rendered.

name.description: Profile name. Becomes the sysctl drop-in filename (/etc/sysctl.d/60-<name>.conf), the gen_name variable, the Incus profile name and the default container prefix, so it is restricted to lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, must not end in a hyphen, and is at most 60 characters. The cap leaves room for the -1/-2 suffix setup.sh appends, which must stay inside Incus's 63-character instance-name limit.

description.description: Free-form note about what this profile installs. Rendered nowhere; read by humans.

image.description: Incus image the container is created from.

runner_user.description: Unprivileged user that owns the runner and the work directory. It must be an account that already exists in the chosen image: the kit creates no users. `setup.sh create` and the first task of prepare.yml fail fast when the account is missing; cloud-init only notices it when the profile has an `env` block, whose group lookup needs the account. It must also equal the PostgreSQL role name, because peer auth compares the OS user to the role. root and postgres are rejected outright.

timezone.description: IANA timezone passed to cloud-init as timezone:. Empty means leave the image default.

locale.description: Locale generated at first boot (locale-gen <locale>), e.g. en_US.UTF-8. Empty means leave the image default. Must match the locale pattern because the value is interpolated into a shell command.

apt.description: APT baseline. Packages are installed by both paths; extra repositories are Ansible-only because cloud-init cannot add signed sources reliably. An explicit null is rejected as ambiguous; omit the block or write {}.

update.description: Maps to cloud-init package_update:. Set false only when the image cache is known fresh.

items.description: Package name. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed and a leading '-' is rejected.

packages.description: Package names installed as-is. No version pins, no wildcards: the profile is a requirement list, not a lockfile. Duplicates collapse to their first occurrence. Packages the enabled services need (postgresql, redis-server) and the locale/timezone tooling (locales, tzdata) are added to the cloud-init package list by the renderer and need not be listed here.

repositories.description: Extra signed APT repositories. Ansible-path only.

name.description: deb822 repository name; also the keyring filename stem. Same pattern as the profile name because it becomes a filename.

key_url.description: URL of the armored signing key. Empty means the repository is unsigned (rare; only for local mirrors).

packages.description: Packages installed once this repository is registered.

python.description: Python tooling. Installs uv, then `uv tool install <name>` as runner_user. Ansible-path only. An explicit null is rejected as ambiguous; omit the block or write {}.

items.description: Tool name. Whitespace is trimmed and a leading '-' is rejected.

uv_tools.description: Tool names resolvable from PyPI, e.g. [ruff, mypy]. Duplicates collapse.

node.description: Node.js tooling installed from NodeSource. Ansible-path only. An explicit null is rejected as ambiguous; omit the block or write {}.

major.description: Node.js major version, e.g. 24. Required whenever npm_globals is non-empty; absent otherwise means Node is not installed at all.

npm_globals.description: Packages installed with `npm install --global`. A non-empty list without node.major is an error: there is no npm to run. Duplicates collapse.

services.description: Services configured on the container. Presence of a block enables it: `postgres: {}` means enabled, and `enabled: false` switches it off. An explicit null is rejected as ambiguous.

postgres.description: PostgreSQL with peer auth over the unix socket: no password is stored anywhere. A present block enables it unless enabled is false.

enabled.description: Provision the server and the peer-auth role. Defaults to true because the block exists.

role.description: Superuser login role created for runner_user, e.g. ubuntu. Defaults to runner_user, and the renderer rejects any other value because peer auth compares the OS user to the role.

redis.description: Redis listening on a unix socket instead of TCP. A present block enables it unless enabled is false.

enabled.description: Rewrite the socket directives in /etc/redis/redis.conf and restart the server. Defaults to true because the block exists.

unixsocket.description: Absolute socket path, e.g. /run/redis/redis-server.sock. The renderer splices this value into a sed expression, so only [A-Za-z0-9._/-] after the leading slash is accepted; quotes, backslashes, '&', spaces and '|' are rejected.

unixsocketperm.description: Octal socket permissions as a quoted string, e.g. "766". A bare integer is rejected: YAML reads 0766 as an integer and loses the octal meaning.

sysctl.description: Kernel tunables written to /etc/sysctl.d/60-<name>.conf as `key = value` lines and applied with sysctl --system. Flat map; values are strings or integers only, because a boolean is ambiguous (1 and 0 are not the only accepted spellings). An explicit null is rejected as ambiguous; omit the block or write {}.

env.description: Environment variables written to /etc/runner-env.sh as `KEY="value"` lines, which both systemd's EnvironmentFile parser and a `set -a; .` shell consumer read back identically. Flat map, values stringified. Not a secret store: the file is readable by the runner's group and is baked into the image. The runner wrapper owns GH_* (it sets GH_TOKEN, GH_URL and the registration API path), the dynamic loader reads LD_*, and the names bash itself reads (PATH, HOME, SHELL, IFS, BASH_ENV, LD_PRELOAD, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, ENV, PYTHONPATH) change how jobs resolve commands, so those keys are rejected. An explicit null is rejected as ambiguous; omit the block or write {}.
